name: Western Apache

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Western Apache (west2615).

notes:
Southern Athabaskan (Apachean) language of east-central Arizona, written in the practical orthography used for San Carlos and White Mountain Apache. Every grapheme value here is the value the cited Wikipedia article gives, whose phonology chart is referenced to Gordon, Potter, Dawson, de Reuse and Ladefoged, 'Phonetic Structures of Western Apache' (IJAL 67.4, 2001). The obstruents carry the Athabaskan three-way laryngeal contrast, and the orthography's voiced-looking letters write the PLAIN (voiceless unaspirated) series, not voiced stops: are /p t k ts tɬ/, are the aspirated /tʰ kʰ tsʰ tʃʰ tɬʰ/, and an apostrophe writes the ejective. is the one exception the source's own alphabet table draws: it gives /dʒ/, a voiced affricate, against plain /ts/.

is /pʰ/ and is rare, mostly in loanwords; there is no ejective bilabial. is /x/ in the source's alphabet table ( [xaʃpɪtɪ́]), while the consonant chart lists both /x/ and /h/ and the orthography does not separate them, so /h/ is kept as the second candidate. Four vowel qualities. Short are /a ɛ ɪ o/ — note that short is lax /ɪ/, not /i/. Length is written by doubling the letter. The long counterparts are /aː ɛː ɪː oː/: the source's vowel table gives the nasal long vowels explicitly as <ąą ęę įį ǫǫ> = /ãː ɛ̃ː ɪ̃ː õː/, which fixes the quality of the oral long vowels by the same rows, and the alphabet table's [pʰɪːʃɪ] and [kʰɛː] show the same /ɪː/ and /ɛː/ directly. The article's vowel CHART instead prints the long close vowel as /iː/; that conflicts with its own <įį> = /ɪ̃ː/ row and with , so /ɪː/ leads here. is in the alphabet table (/u/, [tʰú]) but absent from the 16-vowel chart, so it is a marginal vowel; = /uː/ follows the doubling convention and is attested by neither table. The ogonek writes nasalization and the acute writes high tone. Low tone is unmarked on BOTH sides here, because the source states plainly that low-toned vowels are not marked and its own IPA leaves them bare ( [ʃaʃ], [zas]) — unlike South Slavey, where the descriptions write the low tone out. A long vowel may be written with the acute on either letter or on both, so all three spellings map to one long high nucleus. Three apostrophe characters are accepted (U+02BC, U+2019, ASCII). Two of them occur in the Wiktionary headwords WikiPron scrapes — U+02BC 68 times and U+2019 8 times, with no ASCII apostrophe anywhere in that set — and ASCII is accepted alongside them as the common typing substitute for the modifier letter rather than on attestation. All three write the glottal stop on their own and the ejective after a stop letter. Some of those headwords also write the ogonek with U+031C COMBINING LEFT HALF RING BELOW (, ) rather than U+0328, so the hook form is accepted as the same letter. Two things the sources describe are deliberately NOT encoded. The chart's statement that voiceless unaspirated alveolars are taps intervocalically 'but not stem-initially' needs the stem boundary, which is not recoverable from the orthography, so /t/ keeps its stop value everywhere. And bare is left as /t/+/l/: the barred <ł> is sometimes typed as plain , and after such a spelling an ejective apostrophe is unambiguous (), but a bare sequence also arises across a morpheme boundary (), so only is read as the lateral affricate. Labialized is not a Western Apache letter and the 31-consonant chart has no /kʷ/, so the skeleton's key is dropped; likewise is not a letter of the orthography.

sources.notes: Source of every value in the grapheme table. Its 'Alphabet and pronunciation' table pairs each letter with an IPA value and a worked example: ʼ=/ʔ/, A=/a/, B=/p/, Ch=/tʃʰ/, Chʼ=/tʃʼ/, D=/t/, Dl=/tɬ/, Dz=/ts/, E=/ɛ/, G=/k/, Gh=/ɣ/, H=/x/, I=/ɪ/, J=/dʒ/, K=/kʰ/, Kʼ=/kʼ/, L=/l/, Ł=/ɬ/, M=/m/, N=/n/, O=/o/, P=/pʰ/, S=/s/, Sh=/ʃ/, T=/tʰ/, Tʼ=/tʼ/, Tł=/tɬʰ/, Tłʼ=/tɬʼ/, Ts=/tsʰ/, Tsʼ=/tsʼ/, U=/u/, W=/w/, Y=/j/, Z=/z/, Zh=/ʒ/, plus the vowel rows aa=/aː/, ą=/ã/, á, ą́=/ã́/, ąą=/ãː/, é=/ɛ́/, ę=/ɛ̃/, ę́=/ɛ̃́/, ęę=/ɛ̃ː/, í=/ɪ́/, į=/ɪ̃/, į́=/ɪ̃́/, įį=/ɪ̃ː/, ó, ǫ=/õ/, ǫǫ=/õː/, ǫ́=/ṍ/, ú. Its phonology section is the source of the three-way plain/aspirated/ejective stop series, the 16-vowel chart with contrastive length and nasalization, the statement that aspirated bilabials are rare and mainly in loanwords, the statement that voiceless unaspirated alveolars are taps intervocalically but not stem-initially, and the statement that an acute accent represents high tone while low-toned vowels are not marked. That section cites Gordon et al. 2001 for the consonant facts; the alphabet table itself carries an 'unreferenced section' banner.
